Circuitborn.

“You are not a robot. You are a decision the world keeps making about itself. The networks are alive and they recognize you on sight.”

Firmware of Identity. You do not eat, drink, or sleep. You enter maintenance trance when you rest. You reroll the lowest die on checks against poison and disease, and you are immune to magical sleep.

Attention Resonance. 1/Soma Break, when a creature you can see is intensely focused on you, you may regain either 10 marks you spent this scene or Integrity equal to your tier.

Informational Matrix Sense. You can feel active networks: radio, signal, ritual, rumor.

Line Memory. Choose one Circuitborn line (Exo-Knight, Parallax, Salvage, Synapse). Your line grants Tier powers as you level.

description.value:
“You are not a robot. You are a decision the world keeps making about itself.”

Firmware of Identity. You do not eat, drink, or sleep. You enter maintenance trance when you rest. You reroll the lowest die on checks against poison and disease, and you are immune to magical sleep.

Attention Resonance. 1/Soma Break, when a creature you can see is intensely focused on you (ally or enemy; GM adjudicates), you may regain either (a) 10 marks you spent this scene or (b) Integrity equal to your tier.

Informational Matrix Sense. You can feel active networks: radio, signal, ritual, rumor. You reroll the lowest die on checks to identify surveillance, hidden speakers, encoded messages, or noospheric “attention traps.”

Glitch-Surge. When you drop to 0 Integrity, you can choose to emit a controlled burst of static (no damage, but loud and disorienting) before you fall.

description.value:
Circuitborn Line. The salvage-recursive. Built from the parts of older Circuitborn that didn’t make it. You carry their last instructions in your firmware.

“Nothing in this world is wasted. Some of it is just waiting to be re-purposed.”

Salvage. You are a sentient chassis built around the principle of recovery. Broken things speak to you. So do broken people, when they don’t know they’re doing it.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Construct-Living).
  • Chassis Lean. Your chassis is built around BOD (Body)—expressed primarily through Tier powers.
  • Scrap Memory. You can identify the original purpose of any handheld broken object you touch (1/Soma Break, GM adjudicates depth of detail).

advancement.title: Salvage Tier I
advancement.hint: Gain your Salvage Line Tier I power (Built-In Tools).

rerolls.vs: identifying salvage, pre-collapse tech, or what a broken thing was for

description.value:
“You were born with a wrench in your soul.”

Built-In Tools. You gain a skill rank with the Tinkering aptitude and one artisan tool set of your choice. As part of a Soma Break, you can repair a damaged object or patch armor (GM adjudicates small benefit).

"Give me time, a fire, and something to hit — and then we'll see."

The Soul-Smith runs a forge that does not much care whether you call it a person or a furnace; it answers to heat and intention either way. Mechanically you ride Burn — a 0→8 heat track that climbs when you or a nearby ally takes a hit (the forge stokes itself on other people's bad days) and banks Surge right alongside it. You spend that Surge on four forge-works, and the hotter you run, the harder they land — right up until the furnace bites back.

The Four Works (spent via Surge)

  • Forge-Weld. Lay hands on the breakage and repair an ally — 1d8 + tier integrity. Stoked (Burn 2–3) ×1.5; Overheated (Burn 4+) ×2, and Overheated also costs you 1d6 Stress, because an open forge has opinions about being grabbed.
  • Atonement Crucible. Cleanse a condition off an ally (two while Stoked or hotter) and temper the wound into armor — they gain DR equal to your tier. The bad thing that happened to them is now load-bearing.
  • Furnace of Renewal. Light the aura: allies within 6 squares heal (Burn-scaled) and share your poison/qliphothic resistance for three rounds. Stand near the fire. It is rude not to.
  • Relic of Rebirth. Forge a ward on an ally — the next hit that would drop them is held at 1. While Overheated, instead reforge a fallen ally back to half integrity (once per fight). The forge does not accept "dead" as a final answer. It considers it a draft.

Vent to cool Burn. Out of combat, Forge Works still does the slow miracles — repairing hexes, purifying corrupted Sparks, restoring ruined regions. Those take time, the way good welds do.

description.value:
Sanctified Forge Initiate. You are licensed by the Great Work to hit things until they get better.

  • You gain skill rank with the Plating aptitude and the Faith (Soul) skill (handled by the Soul-Smith class traits).
  • On the campaign layer, when you are physically present in a hex that has structural damage, environmental ruin, or infrastructure loss, your Domain may spend Economy marks to repair or stabilize that hex more efficiently, with you as the narrative focus.

The exact mechanical effect is governed by your hex repair rules, but this feature marks you as a Bad Eden-specific repair engine keyed off Economy marks.

description.value:
Tempered Vitality. Your body has been through the forge and come out with grain aligned.

  • You gain a small mechanical bonus on Body check to resist fatigue, disease, poison, and other long-haul hazards (at the GM’s discretion).
  • In fiction, you don’t cough much, don’t tire easy, and shrug off workshop fumes other people find unbearable.

"What breaks makes the hammer."

Mode: Conquest

The Forge of Victory holds that a defeated enemy is simply raw material that has not been collected yet. You bank Victor's Sparks — a real resource, cap = tier + 1 — whenever a foe of consequence falls within reach of you, then spend Sparks + Surge to forge their ending into your edge. It is exactly as tasteless as it sounds, and it works.

Doctrine (Spark-fueled, spent via Surge)

  • The Victor's Spark. When a foe falls in your presence, bank a Victor's Spark (free). Trophies. Flammable ones.
  • Forged Trophy. Spark + Surge: your next Strike blazes (+tier d6) and an ally gains DR equal to your tier — a weapon and a shield, both made of someone's worst day.
  • Compounded Blow. Spark: your next Strike lands as a max-die critical. The dead, it turns out, hold grudges you can aim.
  • Sundering Stroke. Spark + Surge: your next Strike ignores resistances and leaves the target Staggered. Armor is a suggestion you decline.
  • Banner of the Final Push (L18). Raise the Final Push Standard: a 6-square aura for 1 minute — allies +2 to attacks and defense checks, temporary Integrity each turn, a free 2-square advance on every kill or surrender; enemies roll 3d10 keep lowest 2 against being Shaken. Once per Soma Break; a decisive win echoes 10 Diplomacy or Soft Power marks to your Domain.

Out-of-combat: Standard of Will (raise a standard, allies +1 vs Shaken, +10 Soft Power marks at scene end) and Victory Forge (convert marks after a clean objective) remain the strategic flourishes.

“You don’t just march. You set tempo.”

Your presence and banners teach people how to move like a single thought.

  • When allies begin their turn within 2 squares of you, they gain a +2 squares bonus to their walking speed until the end of that turn.
  • This doesn’t stack with itself, but it does play nicely with other speed increases (GM adjudicates edge cases).

You don’t shout ‘Forward.’ You just start walking and the hex comes with you.

aura.note: Marchwork — +2 squares walk at turn start

description.value:
“You can stitch courage into the air itself.”

When you or an ally you can see within 6 squares succeeds on an attack roll, defense check, or attribute check by 5 or more, you can use your reaction to declare a surge of momentum.

  • Allies of your choice within 3 squares gain temporary Integrity equal to your tier.
  • Those allies also gain a +2 squares bonus to their speed until the end of their next turn.
  • The next Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) check made by any one of the affected creatures before the end of the scene rerolls its lowest die.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your tier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Soma Break.

Domain Echo.. If a Triumph Weave directly helps resolve a conflict without lethal force, your Domain gains +10 Diplomacy marks for the next turn.

activation.condition: When you or an ally within 30 ft succeeds on a roll by 5 or more.

description.value:
“You know how to turn ‘we did it’ into policy.”

Once per Soma Break, when your party achieves a peaceful objective (successful negotiation, retreat, extraction, or surrender) where your symbolism, banners, or presence clearly mattered, you can formalize that victory into the Domain ledger.

  • After that scene resolves, you may convert 10 Intrigue marks into either 10 Diplomacy marks or 10 Soft Power marks for your Domain.
  • This represents codifying rumors, agreements, and personal heroics into actual structural leverage.

“Hold still, I’m sewing your courage back on.”

When a friendly creature you can see within 6 squares fails a defense check, you can use your reaction to tug on the invisible seams.

  • The ally rerolls the defense check and must use the new result.
  • You can use this feature a number of times equal to your tier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Soma Break.

Sometimes all a comeback is missing is one stitch in the right place.

activation.condition: When an ally within 30 ft fails a defense check.

description.value:
“Your forge does not make weapons—your forge makes endings.”

As an action, you can raise the Final Push Standard, a spectral or physical banner that anchors a desperate charge or last stand.

  • You create a 6 squares-radius aura centered on you that lasts for 1 minute and moves with you.
  • Allies in the aura gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and defense check.
  • At the start of each of their turns while in the aura, allies gain temporary Integrity equal to your tier.
  • When an ally in the aura reduces a creature to 0 Integrity or forces a surrender, they can immediately move up to 2 squares without provoking reaction strikes.
  • Enemies in the aura roll 3d10 and keep the lowest 2 on defense checks against being Shaken.

You can use this feature once per a Soma Break.

Domain Echo. If a battle, siege, or parley ends decisively in your Domain’s favor while the banner is active, your Domain gains +10 Diplomacy or Soft Power marks (your choice) for the next turn.

Craft banners the world can stand beneath.

As an action, you can raise a physical or symbolic standard you forged or sanctified (banner, emblem, patchwork flag, welded sign).

  • Until the start of your next turn, allies of your choice within 3 squares of you gain a +1 bonus to defense checks against being Shaken.
  • The standard’s presence lingers in memory. If this scene ends in a clear victory or successful stand where your banner was visibly part of the moment, your Domain gains +10 Soft Power marks (GM’s discretion, once per scene).

People don’t just see cloth. They see permission to keep breathing.

description.value:
Adaptive Defense

Defense is not denial. It is management.

Rules

When you are hit by an attack you can see, you may use your reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your rank bonus + your Violence or Intrigue value (your choice).

🃏 Card — click ▶ when you are hit: it shows the reduction (rank bonus + Violence or Intrigue).

Bound and Bargained

A sealed pact holds itself; you need only keep the terms.

Rules

While your Sealed Pact stance is active, the bindings carry part of your will for you: your Clarity maximum rises by 1.

Requires: Pactkeeper⚙ Applies automatically while the Sealed Pact stance is active: Clarity max +1.

Battlefield Presence

People fight better when you are near.

Rules

Allies within 2 squares of you reroll the lowest die on the first defense checks they make against being Shaken or charmed each combat.

✍ Aura — the GM applies the reroll to the allies' first defense checks against Shaken or charm each combat.
